results.title: Paraguayan president resigns amid bank collapse leaving 3M people without access to bank accounts
results.content: Santiago Peña resigned as president of Paraguay amid the Ueno Bank crisis and was later impeached over an alleged conflict of interest. Vice President Pedro Alliana will take office, while millions of Paraguayans wait to recover their deposits.

results.title: British comedian Russell Brand found guilty of rape and three sexual assaults by London jury
results.content: Russell Brand was convicted of four sexual offences, one rape and three sexual assaults, involving four women between 2005 and 2009 in different locations.

results.title: Greece: Students march in Athens demanding more education funding
results.content: Thousands of pupils, students and teachers marched through central Athens on Thursday in a nationwide push for better-funded schools, joining a protest wave that has spread from France across southern Europe.

results.title: Putin seizes Russian operations of cigarette giant Japan Tobacco International
results.content: The decree transferred JTI’s four factories, around 4,000 employees and roughly 40% of the Russian cigarette market to a state-linked holding company. The latest seizure added to a list that includes Nestlé, Auchan, Leroy Merlin and Metro.

results.title: Ueno Bank collapse in Paraguay prompts President Santiago Peña to resign
results.content: The accounting black hole at Ueno Bank wipes out public funds, leaves thousands without access to their deposits and drives Paraguay into its worst institutional crisis in years.

results.title: France: Up to 55,000 march in Lyon amid clashes and tear gas
results.content: Tens of thousands marched through Lyon area during a nationwide strike over wages and purchasing power. Police charged demonstrators and used tear gas as clashes erupted along the protest route.

results.title: South Korea plans to extend anti-piracy patrols closer to Strait of Hormuz
results.content: Seoul said pirates have recently ventured further from the Somali coast and added that it wanted to send a patrol aircraft to protect merchant ships off Oman while keeping its forces out of the ongoing Iran war.

results.title: Milei and Sánchez exchange a cold greeting at Ibero-American Summit
results.content: Argentine President Javier Milei and Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez exchanged a brief and frosty greeting at the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid on Wednesday. Their encounter comes two weeks after Milei called Sánchez an “unpresentable dictator”.

results.title: France: Mass protests and school blockades mark fourth national strike
results.content: Hundreds of thousands joined a fourth nationwide day of protests across France. Police used tear gas outside a Paris school, while major demonstrations disrupted Marseille and Nantes.

results.title: North Korea tells EU to 'mind its own business' after draft UN resolution on human rights
results.content: The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights said last year that human rights in North Korea have shown no improvement over the past decade and had in fact worsened in many cases.

results.title: Iran: Flames engulf banner depicting US and Israeli leaders
results.content: Demonstrators in Tehran burned a banner depicting US and Israeli leaders during rallies marking the 1979 US embassy takeover. The protests followed a major electoral setback for Donald Trump.

results.title: Drone strike sets Ozon warehouse ablaze in southern Russia
results.content: A fire broke out at an Ozon warehouse in Adygeysk, southern Russia, on Wednesday. The Russian e-commerce giant said the facility had been targeted in a drone attack.

results.title: Ukraine: Russian drone and missile attack sparks fire in Kyiv region
results.content: A Russian strike on a logistics facility in Sofiivska Borshchahivka, in the Kyiv region, injured one man and sparked a major fire, with emergency crews battling the flames following an overnight attack involving 128 drones and two missiles.

results.title: Russia plans ticket surcharge to bankroll struggling aircraft industry
results.content: From 2027, passengers would pay 500 roubles on domestic flights and 1,000 on international flights to fund the lease and operation of 258 Russian-built aircraft, as sactions over Moscow's all-out war in Ukraine continue to bite.

results.title: ‘It would destroy the Democrat Party’: Trump dismisses impeachment threat
results.content: US President Donald Trump has warned that impeaching him would damage the Democratic Party, after Republicans suffered major losses in the midterm elections.

results.title: NASA astronauts cast US election votes from the International Space Station
results.content: In a rare event, three American astronauts voted in Tuesday's US midterm elections from the International Space Station, using advanced links to send electronic ballots to officials on Earth.

results.title: Gaza: Displaced Palestinian builds wind turbine to generate electricity
results.content: A displaced Palestinian in Gaza has built a makeshift wind turbine to bring electricity to tents in Khan Younis. Unable to afford solar panels, he has found a way to harness the wind to power everyday essentials.

results.title: US First Lady Melania Trump to host Ukrainian and Russian officials at White House
results.content: On Wednesday, Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy awarded the first lady a national honour for her role in brokering a partial ceasefire that allowed the evacuation of civilians from a Russian-occupied town.

results.title: New Zealand: Dead whales found as rescuers battle mass stranding
results.content: Volunteers in New Zealand are working to save pilot whales stranded along the Wairarapa coast, near Cape Palliser. At least 14 have been helped back into the water, but many others have died along the remote coastline.

results.title: ‘Zeptoverse’: CERN scientists uncover evidence of extraordinarily rare particle decay
results.content: Scientists at CERN have found evidence of an extraordinarily rare particle decay using the Large Hadron Collider. The process is predicted to occur just once in every 10 billion cases, offering researchers a new way to explore the subatomic world.

results.title: Europe Today: Trump loses Congress. Will he now be even more unpredictable?
results.content: Democrats have seized control of the US Congress in a nationwide rejection of Trump. In Europe, hackers targeted a French blood bank and supermarket fridges, raising fears of a new front in hybrid warfare. Plus: we talk to Reza Pahlavi, one of the main leaders of the opposition to the Tehran regime.

results.title: Crises have taken their classrooms. But education cannot wait
results.content: "Today, the education of 258 million school-aged children worldwide is disrupted by crises," says Reem Alabali Radovan, Germany's Minister for Development in an exclusive op-ed for Euronews. That is why Germany is providing €20 million in funding for education in emergencies over the coming years.

results.title: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 more years for collusion
results.content: Wong rose to prominence during Hong Kong's 2014 protests, known as the Umbrella Movement, and has been in and out of jail since 2017.

results.title: Arab airlines set to record a collective net loss of €3.82 billion in 2026, AACO report reveals
results.content: At its AGM held this week in Doha, the Arab Air Carriers’ Organization raised concerns over EU carbon regulations, as airlines look to boost European connectivity amid ongoing regional uncertainty.

results.content: Zelenskyy visits Madrid to meet Sánchez, Felipe VI and Latin American leaders at the Ibero-American Summit, aiming to boost support for Ukraine and closer ties with Latin America.
